children.label: Title Screen
children.note:
STILL PARTLY THE SAME BUG, found 2026-08-08 while trying to make Qud's chargen drivable: `scene: MainMenu` is a weak positive for the same reason `game_live: false` was. Qud hosts the ENTIRE character-creation flow inside the MainMenu Unity scene, so the scene name is true on the title and true on all five chargen screens. What normally saves it is that the mod reports a chargen WINDOW and via=window wins -- but that report LAGS a transition, and in the gap the scene falls back to MainMenu and this node claims the title. Measured: `hv state` said `Title Screen scene=MainMenu via=scene` while Qud was sitting on QudBuildSummaryModuleWindow, which the very next poll reported correctly. Anything that PLANS off that answer -- which is every `hv goto qud ...` -- can start its route from a screen the app is not on, and that is a large part of why walking Qud's chargen read as random. The honest fix is a first-party report for the title itself (the mod already names every chargen window; it just does not name this one), so the node can match a positive rather than the absence of a chargen window. A settle-until-two-reads-agree in the goto pre-flight would mask it but not fix it.

`{game_live: false}` was an alternative here and is GONE (2026-08-08). It is the absence of bytes on a 0.35s probe, and absence of evidence is not evidence: it is satisfied by every menu screen, so whenever the first-party report was stale or missing this node claimed the title on an inference. Measured twice -- "Title Screen via=live" for 7 minutes while Qud sat on the Modding Toolkit with the mod unloaded, and again on a parked Keybinds screen that had a LIVE game behind it (a parked turn thread publishes no snapshot, so the probe reads false about liveness itself). `gamego` PLANS from that answer, which is what made it expensive.

The asymmetry with in_game's `{game_live: true}` is deliberate, not an oversight. The mod force-publishes a snapshot on connect ONLY when a game is live, so BYTES imply a running game -- a positive, near-sound inference whose worst case is naming in_game while we are on one of its own children. No bytes implies nothing. The positive stays; the negative goes.

With the report stale and no game live, nothing matches and the state is `unknown` -- 'running, screen unknown', which is the honest answer and one the planner can route out of. If an app is ever added with no reporter at all, give it one (the standing rule) rather than restoring this fallback.

children are the SCENE CONTAINERS (each scored individually for 1:1 fidelity); the menu options nest under menu_box (they're both its contents and the nav edges to other scenes). THREE CONCRETE DIVERGENCES FOUND, all measured, none yet fixed: (1) the LEFT LINK COLUMN sits +40 px LOW -- exactly one row pitch. Qud's rows top at y 855/894/932/972, Raves' at 895/934/975/1015; the pitch (39-40) and the x start (65 vs 64) already match, so it is a pure vertical offset of the whole column, and its glyph overlap is 0.0% purely because of it. (2) the BOTTOM HINT LINE is 39% too wide -- Qud x 776..1161 (386 px), Raves x 692..1228 (537 px). (3) the VERSION BLOCK bottom-right is larger, sits ~40 px higher, and carries an extra 'raves 0.2.0' line that Qud has no counterpart for -- it should almost certainly be gated on Settings.one_to_one(). Neither the links nor the hint line use ElliotSans at all (both scored IDENTICALLY with the font hidden), so they are still on the theme face -- likely the same _apply_elliot treatment the menu items get. The REST of the residual is the backdrop art itself, not UI: pure-art regions match only 90.99% (upper right) and 92.47% (upper left) with a mean channel delta of ~6/255 -- a pervasive low-level grade difference spread over the whole screen, which is why it dominates a 97% whole-screen score while no single 120x120 tile holds more than 2.5% of the error. FIXED 2026-08-07, all three re-measured after the change: the LINK COLUMN now tops at y 855/894 against Qud's 855/894 (the 28 px pad it carried was modelling something the diff disproved; dropping it moved the column 54 px, not the 28 its height implied, so the net correction was +2 rather than the -12 arithmetic predicted -- re-measure after a layout change, do not trust the delta). The VERSION CORNER lost the 'raves x.y.z / hv' line (no Qud counterpart, and 1:1 has no business showing it) and now inks at y 1034/1054, exactly Qud's. Whole-screen 97.24 -> 97.26; region-local the links went 89.10 -> 90.16% and the hint 85.23 -> 86.78%. TWO METRIC TRAPS recorded because both read as failures and are not: (a) 'glyph overlap' still reports 0.0% for the link column even with the rows pixel-aligned -- Qud draws those links too dim for a >120 ink threshold to find ANY Qud pixel to agree with, so use local contrast against a blurred copy for text over painted art; (b) the version corner's region score DROPPED 93.94 -> 88.79 while becoming more correct, because our text moved off empty background and onto Qud's own text, and Raves deliberately renders that corner brighter than Qud's near-illegible build line. children.note: DECODED FROM IL + VERIFIED LIVE (2026-08-06). The on-screen hint 'Ctrl+Click-Paint from palette' is MISLEADING: painting is not a click. All three drag verbs live in OnDragMove, each gated on a modifier read with Input.GetKey: SHIFT (LeftShift/RightShift) -> region select (sets isDragging/_dragStart, Rect min/max, RenderSelectionFrame); CTRL (LeftControl/RightControl) -> PAINT (raycast -> MapFileRegion.GetOrCreateCellAt -> MapFileCell.Objects.Add -> UndoStack.Push -> RenderMap); NO MODIFIER -> camera pan (LetterboxCamera.SetPositionImmediately). DRIVING IT SYNTHETICALLY IS ONLY PARTLY SOLVED, and the honest numbers matter: Ctrl+drag DOES paint — objects appear on the canvas and the count climbs across runs — but it is INTERMITTENT, not reliable. Identical gestures at the same coordinates sometimes place an object (+57 px, one sprite) and sometimes place nothing. An earlier claim here that paint simply 'works' was too confident; it lands often enough to prove the verb, not often enough to script against yet. HOLD DURATION MEASURED: `hv drag --hold` sets the pause between press and first move. Longer is WORSE — at 0.5s and 1.2s a Ctrl+drag painted NOTHING in any trial, while the 0.08 default paints some of the time. A long press before movement stops registering as a drag at all. children.label: Stranded stage (game over, view stuck)
children.note:
A game that ENDED whose view never returned to the menu: The.Game is gone (`live: false`) while _ActiveGameView is still `Stage`. It used to read as In-Game, because in_game listed `Stage` among its scenes, and that mislabelling did the real damage: `hv goto qud in_game` from here planned ZERO steps and reported ok, so every 'retry on a fresh load' re-tested the same dead game. That is what disguised the Classic-save ABANDON bug as progressive process ageing for most of a session -- the retries were never reloading anything. Recorded evidence, 30 runs entered here: all 10 `goto in_game` calls planned 0 steps and returned ok; the other 20 failed and left the state exactly as they found it. It is ABSORBING -- 20/20 with no self-recovery -- which is why its only exit is a restart.

TOP LEVEL, deliberately: as a child of in_game it would sit on in_game's path, and `assert node=in_game` tolerates landing deeper, so the edge that is supposed to catch 'the game never started' would pass here.

NOT included: `StageWindow`, the other stage-ish scene the reporter can emit (view went vague, window still the stage). It is also always not-live, but it behaves differently in the record -- both runs that drove from it reached MainMenu, so it looks transient rather than absorbing, and naming it here would restart Qud for a state that settles on its own. Left as-is with the evidence written down rather than guessed at.

costs._note: What a step costs us -- not seconds, but how much we want to AVOID it. Overlays plan.DEFAULT_COSTS. Bridge commands are near-free and never miss; click_text is dear because OCR is the one class that goes flaky, and a missed match does not fail cleanly, it clicks the wrong thing; launch is slow; restart always works and is therefore the last thing the planner should reach for.

preflight.note: GHOST MODAL self-heal. UIManager.popupMessages is a free pool and a RELEASED copy still looks live, so the mod can report scene=PopupMessage with nothing on screen -- and Qud swallows every key while it thinks a modal is up. That is what made the equipment key look broken for a whole session. It is a CONDITION sitting on top of a state, not a state: modelling it as a node would double the graph and as an edge it would need a self-loop, which a shortest-path search cannot use. So it runs before planning, and the plan is made against what is actually there. This one declaration replaced sixteen copy-pasted dismiss steps across the status-tab recipes.

transitions.note: COLD START. No `unless_running` guard any more: the planner only picks this edge from `off`, which is exactly what that flag was hand-checking on every run.

RESTART IS THE ONLY WAY OUT, and this edge exists to say so explicitly rather than let the route fall through to the universal `* -> title` hatch -- where picking it is supposed to mean 'a real exit edge is missing'. Here nothing is missing: the game object is gone, so no first-party command can rebuild it, and 20 recorded drive attempts from this state changed nothing. Priced the same as the hatch because it costs the same; nothing routes THROUGH a stranded stage, so the price only affects getting out.

uiback closes it -- measured. `exact` on the verify because control_mapping is a CHILD of in_game, so the default tolerance (landing deeper is fine) would be satisfied by the very screen this edge exists to LEAVE.

MEASURED 2026-08-09, both screens, after a session lost to the belief that neither had an exit. Everything OS-level fails on them -- an HID Escape left the Book up, and so did `hv click` and a second press of the button that opened it. So does the mod's LEGACY key queue (`bridge key key=escape`), which is the surprise: the Book is a MODERN window (BookScreen) wearing a legacy view name, so it reads neither. `uiback` closes both, by different rungs of its own ladder -- the Book through `FireInputButtonEvent(CancelButton)`, the Looker through the last rung's queue-injected Cancel, which `Keyboard.metaMousecommands` maps 'Meta:Cancel' -> Keys.Escape and the getvk loop reads as the Escape it is waiting for. No `exact` needed: both are children of in_game, and _drive_route attaches `not_within` to a climbing edge by itself. Landing on a status screen (the Book can be opened from one) is a legitimate arrival, which is why `exact` would be WRONG here even though control_mapping wants it.

The terminal is ONE CHANNEL all the way down, so it exits through its own mirror command rather than the generic uiback: `cyber action=quit` marshals onto the uiQueue and calls the live CyberneticsTerminalScreen's own Exit(). That closes the whole screen from any depth -- verified from the Upgrade Your License SUB-menu, not just the root -- which matters because a back-one-level exit would satisfy nothing and leave the route to loop. No `exact` on the verify: this is a climbing edge (cyber_terminal is inside in_game) and _drive_route attaches `not_within` itself.

The RAVES edge sends the same command to the same mod, and that is not a copy-paste slip: Raves does not own this screen, it mirrors it. The overlay closes when Qud's does, so the only way for Raves to leave is to close Qud's terminal -- exactly what Raves' own quit button does (CyberOverlay emits {action:quit} onto this command). Without this edge Raves' single route out was `unknown -> title` via RESTART, cost 143, over a live game.

THE SAFETY NET, and the actual lesson of the Book. Both screens above are nodes now, but the failure was never really about those two: an unmodelled Qud screen has no edges, so the planner's only route was the `*`->title RESTART -- which CLAUDE.md already names as the signal that a real exit is missing, and which cost a save reload to obey. Qud's screens overwhelmingly close on their own first-party cancel, so trying that BEFORE reaching for a restart is right for the next unmodelled screen too, and it costs 1 against the restart's 120. `port_open` because a bridge command means nothing without the mod. It cannot lie about arriving: `unknown` is not inside in_game, so the default verify is a real check -- if uiback closes nothing we are still unmatched and the planner re-plans onto the restart it would have taken anyway.

THE UNIVERSAL ESCAPE HATCH, and the reason there is always a route. Every state that has no modelled exit -- the tombstone (injected Esc is ignored there), an unmodelled modern screen, or `unknown` after a cheap poll -- can still reach the title by restarting. Cost 120 keeps it last: the planner takes any chain of first-party moves over it, and picking it AT ALL is the signal that a real exit edge is missing.

steps.note: Answered ON ARRIVAL, not on a timer: the old blind version slept 1.2s between sends, and a socket write to the mod succeeds whether or not a modal is up, so the step could not fail and the real fault surfaced 45s later as the verify. See engine._qud_command_chain.

SETTLE. Answering the quit confirms over the bridge can leave a PopupMessage reported for a while after the game has actually ended — and PopupMessage is one of the scenes in_game's detector claims, so the edge verified 'still In-Game' and failed while Qud was already on its way to the menu (it read MainMenu ~40s later, unaided). Driving popups over the bridge is what leaves them, so the edge that drives them clears them. Conditional, so it is a no-op when nothing is up — an unconditional uiback at the MainMenu would hit the menu's own Cancel.

transitions.note:
LEAVE A LIVE GAME, first-party throughout: CmdQuit goes through Qud's own command path and the confirms are answered BY BUTTON via the mod, so nothing here depends on synthesized keys -- which Qud's modern UI ignores outright. Yes to 'are you sure you want to quit', then NO to 'do you want to save first': Yes would overwrite the fixture save with whatever state the harness drove the character into, destroying the reference every parity capture is measured against. (Qud DISCARDS that second answer -- decompiled XRLCore assigns DialogResult.No and then ignores the prompt's return -- but answer it correctly anyway; the prompt is real and must be cleared.)

Raves opens the status overlay with F2 and you pick a TAB. It DOES define Qud's per-screen letter bindings now (MainFrame.STATUS_TAB_KEYS: k/x/e/n/j/q plus Tab and I) -- but they are unreachable while 1:1 is on, because Raves FORWARDS letters to Qud. Measured on Windows 2026-08-08 with both apps in-game: f2 opens the overlay, k/x/e/n/q do nothing through either delivery path, and j raises a PopupMessage in QUD -- i.e. the key arrives and Qud's own binding fires. So this is a routing fact about 1:1 mode, identical on both platforms, NOT a Windows input problem: the F2 + tab-click form is the right edge on macOS too. (An earlier version of this note said Raves lacked the bindings; that was true when it was written and is not now.) Tab x MEASURED off the live strip at 1920x1080; y=136 is the strip's text row (the messagelog edge already used it). Qud's Commands.xml default binding for this screen. MEASURED ON macOS 2026-08-08, which narrows the reason: the letter keys DO reach MainFrame here -- `hv key raves k` opens Skills, and the whole-tree tour arrived at all eight status nodes through them, twice. So 1:1's letter-forwarding is NOT identical on both platforms. The reason this edge is one form rather than a per-OS seam is simpler: F2 + tab-click works on BOTH, and the letter keys only work on one.
